summary: If no element of B_f moved g_f into the level, every term of the Poincaré series would vanish at g.

steps.claim: Suppose no r ∈ B_f has r·g_f in the level. Then for every rational γ of the Bessel group and every a, the finite part of inclX(a⁻¹η)·γ lies in B_f, so it does not move g_f into the level.
steps.lean:
by_contra!; have (γ : Y.ratBessel) a :=
    this _ (Y.snd_mem_besselFin (mul_mem (Y.inclX_mem_besselGroup (a⁻¹ * η)) γ.2.2))

steps.claim: Hence every cut-off term cutBessel(a, γg) vanishes (its finite condition fails), so the Poincaré series vanishes at g, contradicting hg.
